compiler_summary: Three sources (S001, S002, S003) present a thesis that the hyperscaler AI CapEx cycle is structurally broken, predicting $150-200B in write-downs between 2026-2028. Core claims include: GPU utilization below break-even thresholds, phantom asset problems from rapid obsolescence, and demand projections being overestimated. Key epistemic voids center on actual firm-level utilization, depreciation schedules, and financing costs. Tensions exist between the thesis's bearish predictions and market consensus on AI CapEx rationality, demand growth, and GPU utilization.

epistemic_voids.blocking: Cannot verify the utilization gap claim at firm level; hyperscalers do not disclose fleet-wide billable GPU utilization
epistemic_voids.unknown: Actual billable GPU utilization rates across individual hyperscalers (Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon)
epistemic_voids.why_it_matters: The thesis's central argument relies on utilization being 35-55% at inference clusters and 52% for Microsoft, but this may vary significantly by company

epistemic_voids.blocking: Cannot verify which demand projection is more accurate without external data
epistemic_voids.unknown: Actual enterprise AI adoption rates and inference demand projections for 2026-2027
epistemic_voids.why_it_matters: The thesis predicts 180% YoY growth vs consensus 350% and only 2-3x cumulative growth by 2027 instead of 10x; the failure cascade depends on adoption stalling

epistemic_voids.blocking: Cannot verify the phantom asset problem magnitude firm by firm
epistemic_voids.unknown: Actual depreciation schedules used by individual hyperscalers for GPU assets
epistemic_voids.why_it_matters: The thesis assumes 4-5 year straight-line depreciation but schedules may differ across firms, affecting the phantom asset problem magnitude

epistemic_voids.blocking: Cannot verify leverage amplifier calculation per firm
epistemic_voids.unknown: Actual cost of debt financing for each hyperscaler for AI CapEx specifically
epistemic_voids.why_it_matters: The thesis uses SOFR+250bps but actual spreads may differ significantly; the leverage amplifier calculation is sensitive to this input

epistemic_voids.blocking: Hyperscalers do not disclose inference/training workload split
epistemic_voids.unknown: Actual proportion of GPU capacity deployed for inference vs training across the fleet
epistemic_voids.why_it_matters: Utilization patterns differ dramatically between inference (35-55%) and training (80%+ spikes); fleet mix determines aggregate utilization

epistemic_voids.blocking: Cannot verify the zero-revenue capacity claim
epistemic_voids.unknown: Actual percentage of capacity that is unutilized and generating zero revenue vs. generating some revenue at low utilization
epistemic_voids.why_it_matters: The thesis states 40% of capacity is stranded but the source of this figure is unclear; zero-revenue vs. low-revenue capacity has different financial implications

immutable_ground_truth.statement: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 list price is $30,000-$40,000 USD per GPU.
NVIDIA H100 thermal design power is 700W.
AWS p5.48xlarge on-demand price is $98.32/hr for the full instance, approximately $12.29 per GPU per hour.
The SOFR rate estimate for March 2026 is 4.30%.
Microsoft FY2025 CapEx guidance is $80B USD.
The source claims internal GPU utilization at inference clusters runs 35-55% on average.
The source claims NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture (GB200) renders Hopper (H100) economically obsolete within 18 months of deployment.
The source states Microsoft CapEx/FCF ratio expanded from 0.35x (FY2022) to 0.85x (FY2025).
The source gives SOFR at 4.3% + 250bps = 6.8% effective cost of debt-financed CapEx.
The source contains a specific prediction: aggregate hyperscaler AI CapEx guidance cut by 28-35% from peak 2025 levels by Q4 2027.
The source contains a specific prediction: Microsoft will take $18-25B in accelerated depreciation write-downs between Q2 2026 and Q4 2027.
The source contains a specific prediction: hyperscaler AI segment operating margins compress 600-900bps from FY2025 levels.
The source contains a specific prediction: NVIDIA data center revenue will miss FY2027 consensus by 22-30%.
Typical hyperscaler GPU cluster utilization is 40-60% (midpoint 52%).

provenance.summary: Thesis document arguing that hyperscaler AI CapEx cycle is structurally broken, predicting $150-200B in write-downs across Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Amazon between 2026-2028. Core argument: utilization gap is structural (not cyclical), depreciation mismatch on H100 silicon creates phantom asset problem, demand curve is misread, and leverage amplifies capital destruction. Includes quantitative model (Z = f(X,Y)) with specific predictions and Python test harness.

This source provides a table of quantitative variables and estimates relevant to AI capex, including hyperscaler spending, GPU pricing and specifications, operational costs, financial rates, and market forecasts. It includes derived calculations such as break-even utilization and stranded capex estimates, as well as historical precedent data.

This source presents a thesis arguing that the hyperscaler AI CapEx cycle ($300B+ annually) is structurally broken, predicting $150-200B in write-downs between 2026-2028 across Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Amazon. It provides a mathematical model (Z = f(X,Y)) and specific quantitative predictions about CapEx cuts, accelerated depreciation, margin compression, and NVIDIA revenue misses.
